title: Lindy Effect
equation: Expected Remaining Life ≈ Time Already Survived
hook: Every year there's a new tool everyone swears by. Most of them are gone in two.
statement: The longer something has already lasted, the longer it's likely to keep lasting.
explainer: Bookkeeping, sales calls, word of mouth. They've survived for ages for a reason. The shiny new tactic hasn't proven anything yet, so treat it like a test, not a foundation.
sop: List the tools, tactics, and strategies your business leans on.
Write down how long each one has been around.
Build your core on the ones with long track records.
Run the new stuff as small, cheap experiments.
Check back yearly and promote whatever survives.
equation_example: A business model that's worked for 8 years should last roughly 8 more. A tool that's 6 months old, maybe 6 more months. Time Already Survived ≈ Expected Remaining Life. Longer track record, longer future. Short track record, still an experiment.
question: Sort your current bets into two lists: proven for years, and riding a trend.
closing_statement: What's lasted a long time tends to keep lasting.
caption:
Principle Nº 321: Lindy Effect

Every year there's a new tool everyone swears by. Most of them are gone in two.

The longer something has already lasted, the longer it's likely to keep lasting.
